start: Think of each word as a place on a map, with a road to every dictionary word that differs from it in exactly one position: `hit` to `hot` changes only the middle letter. You want the route with the fewest roads, listed word by word with both ends included, so 4 moves is 5 words.

Breadth-first search from `start`, with a queue and a dict from each word reached to the word it was reached from. Generate neighbours instead of storing them: every position, every letter from `a` to `z`, kept only if the result is in the dictionary set. Record a word when you queue it, never later: the first time a word is reached is along a shortest route.

start.text: Validate before the shortcuts: bad lengths or characters raise `ValueError`, then equal endpoints give `[start]`, then an `end` missing from the dictionary gives `[]`. The shape:

test_shortest_and_valid: `hit` to `cog` through `hot, dot, dog, lot, log, cog`: the path must have 5 words, start with `hit`, end with `cog`, use only dictionary words after the first, and change exactly one letter per step. Either route, through `dot, dog` or `lot, log`, passes.

The answer is the list of words, not a count: `len(path)` fails on `4` or `5`. A path built by following parents from `cog` comes out backwards, so reverse it. A depth-first search can find a longer route; only breadth-first order guarantees the fewest moves.
test_missing_and_unreachable: Both calls must return `[]`, an empty list, not `None`. First `cog` is not in the dictionary `["hot"]`; then it is, in `["hot", "cog"]`, but `hot` and `cog` differ in two letters, so nothing connects them. When the queue runs dry, return `[]`.
test_identity_direct_duplicates: `word_ladder("a", "a", [])` must be `["a"]`: equal endpoints are zero moves, even with an empty dictionary, so check `start == end` before checking that `end` is in the dictionary. Then `("a", "b", ["b", "b"])` must be `["a", "b"]`: a repeated word is still one word.
test_validation: Four calls must raise `ValueError`: two empty endpoints, endpoints `"a"` and `"bb"` of different lengths, a dictionary word `"C"` that is not lowercase, and a dictionary word `"zz"` of the wrong length. Check every dictionary word, not only the endpoints.

A shortcut would answer each of them first: `""` and `""` are equal, so an early `[start]` fires, and in the other three the end is not in the dictionary, so an early `[]` fires. Validate first, then take the shortcuts.

TypeError: `word[i] = letter` raises this, because strings cannot be changed in place. Build each neighbour from slices: the part before `i`, the new letter, and the part after `i`.
`len(path)` in “Shortest and valid” fails on a number: return the list of words on the path, both ends included, not the count of moves.
KeyError: Following the parents back from `end` reached a word with no entry. Put `start` in the parent dict before the search, with `None` as its parent, and stop the walk when you reach it.

stopped: A queue that never empties means words are queued again after they were reached. With `["hot", "cog"]`, a loop that does not skip the letter already in place makes `hot` its own neighbour, and without a record of reached words it goes back in forever. Record each word when you queue it, and skip it after that.

If the search found `end` but the call does not return, check the walk back along the parents: it has to stop at `start`. If `start` is stored as its own parent, a walk that waits for `None` goes round forever.
passing: All passing. Try the README's first follow-up, every shortest path instead of one: what must each word remember about its parents, and when is it safe to stop? Then time a big dictionary as your own input, every three-letter word from `aaa` to `zzz`, with `word_ladder("aaa", "zzz", words)`.
